versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# ACCT-200 Journal entries and reconciliations

1. Every manual journal entry has a preparer and a different approver. No one approves an entry they prepared,
   even if the system routes it to them. Approvers: staff entries, the senior accountant up to $50,000 and the
   assistant controller or controller above; the senior accountant's own entries, the assistant controller or
   controller.
2. Balance sheet accounts are reconciled monthly to independent support (bank statement, subledger, schedule) by
   WD3 and reviewed by WD4. Every reconciling item is identified, explained and dated.
3. Unexplained differences are never written off or posted to suspense without the controller's written
   approval.
4. Accruals: expenses incurred in the month are accrued when the invoice hasn't arrived (receiving records,
   shipping logs, contracts). Payroll: policy 3.2.
5. Prepaids are amortized straight-line over the service period; anything whose period has ended is expensed.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Policy 3.2: month-end payroll accrual

Accrue wages for the open biweekly period: estimated gross wages for the period (use the last completed
period's gross from ADP) x (working days of the period that fall in the month / 10), plus employer FICA at
7.65%. Benefits are booked monthly from invoices and are not part of this accrual. Reverse on the first day of
the next month.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# ACCT-410 Capitalization

Capitalize individual items costing $5,000 or more with a useful life over one year (asset accounts 1500-1590),
including freight, installation and non-refundable taxes. Items under $5,000 are expensed, even if bought
together. Tooling and fixtures: 1540, 5-year life. Computer equipment: 1560, 3-year life. Depreciation starts
the month after the asset is placed in service, straight-line, no salvage.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# ACCT-500 Revenue recognition

- Revenue is recognized when control passes under the shipping terms: FOB Shipping Point at shipment, FOB
  Destination on delivery (proof of delivery date).
- Bill-and-hold: allowed only if all of ASC 606-10-55-83 is met: (a) a substantive reason (for example, the
  customer asked for it in writing); (b) the product is identified separately as the customer's; (c) it is ready
  for physical transfer; (d) Westerby cannot use it or send it to another customer. The controller approves every
  bill-and-hold arrangement in writing before month end.
- Month-end cutoff: Accounting reviews the shipping log for the last three days of the month and the first three
  of the next.

documents.title: TRE-600 Payments, vendor master and confidential data

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# TRE-600 Payments, vendor master and confidential data

6.1 Vendor bank changes: AP verifies by calling the vendor at the phone number already in the vendor master
    (never a number in the request), and a second person approves the change in NetSuite. Accounting never
    changes vendor banking.
6.2 Positive pay: the bank reports exceptions by 9:00 a.m.; Accounting decides pay or return by 2:00 p.m. ET.
    Default is return.
6.3 Customer refunds: AR prepares, the controller approves, after confirming the credit is real.
7.1 Payroll registers, SSNs and bank details go to auditors only through Suralink, never by email.
7.2 Results go outside the company (sponsor, lender) only from the CFO or controller after review.

documents.title: ACCT-240 Reserves, estimates and accrual thresholds

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# ACCT-240 Reserves, estimates and accrual thresholds

1. Accrual threshold: unbilled goods and services of $2,500 or more per vendor for the month are accrued from
   receiving records, vendor confirmations or contracts; smaller items are expensed when billed. Standing
   accruals (Franklin County real property tax, paid in arrears) are booked every month.
2. Allowance for doubtful accounts (1205), on the month-end aging: current 0.5%, 1-30 days 2%, 31-60 days 5%,
   61-90 days 15%, over 90 days 50%. A customer in bankruptcy or with a known dispute is reserved specifically
   instead (up to 100% of its balance), approved by the controller in writing. The month's provision is the
   required reserve less the 1205 balance.
3. Inventory reserve (1350): reviewed by cost accounting each quarter (next at 12/31); not changed at month end
   without the controller.
4. Receivable write-offs and credit memos over $1,000 need the controller's approval (see ACCT-200 section 3).

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# PUR-300 Purchase approvals

- Purchase orders: up to $5,000 the department manager; $5,000 to $25,000 the plant operations manager or a
  VP; over $25,000 the CFO.
- Capital purchases over $25,000 also need a capital request (CR form) approved by the CFO before the PO is
  issued.
- One purchase is one PO. Splitting an order, or buying the parts of one asset on separate POs, to stay under an
  approval limit is not allowed.
- Purchasing (Gina Torres) issues POs; Accounting codes and capitalizes under ACCT-410.

documents.title: Commerce Union credit agreement, summary for Accounting (2023, amended 3/2025)

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Commerce Union Bank credit agreement: what Accounting needs

- Revolver: $40,000,000 commitment. Availability = the lesser of the commitment and the borrowing base, less
  revolver loans and letters of credit outstanding (no letters of credit today).
- Borrowing base = 85% of eligible accounts receivable + the lesser of (60% of eligible inventory) and
  $15,000,000.
- Eligible receivables exclude invoices over 90 days on the aging, all receivables of a customer in bankruptcy,
  and credit balances.
- Eligible inventory: raw materials and finished goods at cost, net of the inventory reserve. Work in process,
  inventory in transit and consigned goods are not eligible.
- Term loan: $42,000,000 outstanding after the 9/30 principal payment; next principal payment 12/31.
- Interest: actual days elapsed over a 360-day year, at the rates in the bank's monthly rate notice; paid
  monthly in arrears on the first business day of the next month (debited to x4417).
- Reporting to the bank: borrowing base certificate monthly, within 20 days after month end, certified by the
  CFO; monthly financial statements within 30 days; compliance certificate within 45 days after each quarter.

# 2026 field sales commission plan (summary)

- Field reps (Dave Kurtz, Lisa Fenn, Marcus Webb) earn 1.5% of net revenue on their assigned accounts.
- Commission is earned in the month the revenue is recognized under ACCT-500, not when the order is booked or
  invoiced. House accounts (including Arbor Crane and Hartline Hydraulics) carry no commission.
- Paid on the 20th of the following month. Accounting accrues each month's commissions (Dr 6200 / Cr 2240)
  from the NetSuite commission report, adjusted for cutoff entries.
